assumptions.name: BPR cost curve
assumptions.value: t(x) = t0 (1 + 0.15 (x / c)^4) on grid links; the conventional values, also the values the Sioux Falls file assumes

assumptions.name: Practical margin delta
assumptions.value: 0.01 relative excess, a convention fixed by the study before any run, not an externally grounded threshold

assumptions.name: Demand level rho
assumptions.value: multiple of the total demand at which free-flow loading first brings a link to capacity

assumptions.name: Grid family grid-v1
assumptions.value: n by n lattice, t0 uniform on [1, 3] minutes, capacity uniform on [600, 1800] veh/h, 12 OD pairs with Dirichlet weights

assumptions.name: Behaviour
assumptions.value: static deterministic assignment with perfect information; synthetic travellers are not people

assumptions.name: Solver of record
assumptions.value: path-based gradient projection, stopping at relative gap 1e-6 or 20,000 sweeps

assumptions.name: Partial compliance MIX(c)
assumptions.value: a share c follows the scaled system-optimal path flows; the rest reaches equilibrium around them

limitations: Synthetic networks: the primary result rests on seeded lattices with 12 OD pairs; Sioux Falls is one small test network. Nothing transfers to real cities or navigation products.
Static deterministic assignment: no time dynamics, queues, departure-time choice, signals or stochastic route choice.
Cost curvature: with linear-in-flow costs (S2) the excess falls below the margin; the result holds for quartic costs only.
Light demand: at rho = 1 the median excess is below the margin at both grid sizes.
One solver: the Frank-Wolfe reference failed to converge on most instances, so there is no independent solver check on grids.
Exact checks: EXP-001 and EXP-002 are contradicted under their frozen rule; the 1e-10 evidence is exploratory and post hoc.
Pre-freeze exposure: exploratory values of the primary-cell analogue were seen before the freeze (disclosure C4).
Shared instances: EXP-004 and EXP-005 reuse EXP-003 instances and are not independent replications.
The margin delta = 0.01 is a study convention; the OD count and distance rule were never varied.
question: Can individually optimal routing worsen collective travel time? FLOW measures the gap between user-equilibrium and system-optimal total travel time on a Braess network, seeded synthetic grids and one test network (Sioux Falls). It is not a reconstruction of any navigation product and makes no prediction for any real city.
status_label: Preregistered simulation study. Protocol v1.0 frozen by the owner on 2026-11-24; all six confirmatory experiments complete; manuscript draft, not peer-reviewed; the owner's full-text review is pending (M6).
